text:
Vincent Trocheck's first season in Utah has a strange shape. The Mammoth trust him more every week: he's averaging 20:24 over his last ten games, almost four minutes more than before, including 26:36 against St. Louis. The goals have not followed. He has none in ten games, on 2.8 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and three all season on 5.1 expected.

That's the hopeful read, and our numbers lean toward it. The chances are his usual ones, and Utah takes 58.8% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, better than when he sits. He has also thrown 53 hits, so he's hardly hiding. The worry is narrower. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best (99th percentile competition) and giving up more chances than most forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found 53% of his shots came off the rush, so watch whether those transition looks start finishing. That's where his game has always lived.
